title: The Red Kite
source: Original passage written for this demonstration (no ReadWorks content)
content:
Mia found the red kite in the back of the closet. Its paper was torn, and the string was tangled into a hundred tiny knots.

"I can fix it," she told her grandfather. "Will you help me?"

Grandpa smiled. He brought tape, scissors, and a ball of new string. Together they mended the tear and untied the knots, one by one. It took the whole afternoon.

The next morning, the wind was strong and steady. Mia ran across the field with the kite behind her. For a moment it dragged on the grass. Then it lifted, wobbled, and rose higher and higher until it looked as small as a bird.

"You did it!" Grandpa called.

Mia held the string tightly and laughed. The red kite danced in the blue sky, and she did not want to let go.
